items.title: Google unveils Gemini 4 Carbon, its top model, limited to cyber defenders for now
items.summary: Google launched Gemini 4 Carbon, which it pitches as its most capable model for cybersecurity and long coding tasks. Access starts with a small group of cyber defenders via the Fairwind Program; introductory pricing is $2/$10 per million input/output tokens, rising to $4/$20.
items.whyItMatters: Not usable for the tutor yet and the post says nothing about voice or French, but it sets a new price and capability ceiling to watch for when it reaches general availability.

items.title: Anthropic launches tools showing enterprises what their Claude spend is buying
items.summary: New reporting shows each team's output, cost and workflow friction, with recommendations and pooled group budgets. Anthropic is using it to demonstrate ROI to large customers.
items.whyItMatters: Worth knowing as a model for per-session cost and usage dashboards if the tutor ever needs to track spend per learner.

items.title: Microsoft's 10-Q shows ~$10B quarterly revenue from OpenAI arrangements
items.summary: Microsoft reported about $10B from OpenAI-related deals in the quarter ended Sept 30, nearly 11% of revenue, with $7.2B in receivables. Its OpenAI ownership stake fell to about 24%.
items.whyItMatters: Shows how entangled and capital-heavy the OpenAI ecosystem is, relevant to Romain's reliance on OpenAI Realtime pricing and stability.
